Event title: Founding of Santiago de Leon de Caracas

Description: The Duke of Parma is defeated near Nijmegen by an Anglo-Dutch force led by Maurice of Orange.
People involved: Duke of Parma; Maurice of Orange

Description: Henry IV of France publicly converts from Protestantism to Roman Catholicism.
James VI and I and Anne of Denmark are crowned in Westminster Abbey.
Event title: Coronation of James VI and I and Anne
People involved: James VI and I; Anne of Denmark

Description: Troops led by Ali ibn Abu Talib clashed with those led by Muawiyah I.
People involved: Ali ibn Abu Talib; Muawiyah I

Description: Byzantine Emperor Nikephoros I was killed and his heir Staurakios was seriously wounded.
An alliance of Christian troops from Navarre and León was routed by Muslim forces.
During a Hoftag organized by Henry VI, the building collapsed and many attending nobles drowned in sewage pits below.
Pope Clement V recognized Henry VII as King of the Romans.
Event title: Henry VII recognized King of the Romans

Description: Krishnadevaraya became Emperor of Vijayanagara, beginning the regeneration of the Vijayanagara Empire.
Francisco Pizarro González was appointed governor of Peru.

Notes: The location is stated as probably Oregon or Washington.
Description: Francis Drake discovered a “fair and good” bay on the Pacific Northwest coast, probably in Oregon or Washington.
Event title: Drake discovers a Pacific Northwest bay

Description: The northern Low Countries declared their independence from the Spanish king, Philip II.
The rural population of Tyrol defeated and drove the Bavarian Prince-Elector Maximilian II Emanuel out of North Tyrol, preventing the Bavarian Army from marching on Vienna as planned.
The first recorded women's cricket match took place near Guildford, England.
A French army under Marshal d'Estrées defeated a smaller British-German army under the Duke of Cumberland.
British forces defeated the French and took control of the Gulf of Saint Lawrence.
The Second Continental Congress established the office that later became the United States Post Office Department, with Benjamin Franklin as Postmaster General.
The emigration of Christians from Crimea in 1778 began.
Event title: Emigration of Christians from Crimea begins

Description: New York ratified the United States Constitution and became the 11th state of the United States.
The Surrey Iron Railway, arguably the world's first public railway, opened in south London.
The Swedish–Norwegian War began.
José de San Martín arrived in Guayaquil, Ecuador, to meet Simón Bolívar.
People involved: José de San Martín; Simón Bolívar

Notes: First day of a three-day battle.
Description: The first day of the three-day Battle of Dervenakia took place between an Ottoman force led by Mahmud Dramali Pasha and a Greek Revolutionary force led by Theodoros Kolokotronis.
Siward, Earl of Northumbria, invades Scotland and defeats Macbeth, King of Scotland, somewhere north of the Firth of Forth.
Friedrich Barbarossa arrives at Niš, the capital of Serbian King Stefan Nemanja, during the Third Crusade.
At the Battle of Basian, the Kingdom of Georgia defeats the Sultanate of Rum.
Historical entity: Kingdom of Georgia; Sultanate of Rum

Description: Philip II of France decisively defeats Imperial, English and Flemish armies, effectively ending John of England's Angevin Empire.
People involved: Philip II of France; John of England
Historical entity: Kingdom of France; England; Flemish armies

Notes: The event is attributed to Edward Gibbon and is usually considered the founding day.
Description: According to Edward Gibbon, Osman I invades the territory of Nicomedia for the first time, usually considered the founding day of the Ottoman state.
The Ottomans achieve a decisive victory over the Byzantines, opening Bithynia for Turkish conquest.
The Jesuit priest Francis Xavier's ship reaches Japan.
The English Parliament passes the second Navigation Act, requiring goods bound for the American colonies to be sent in English ships from English ports.
The Battle of Killiecrankie is a victory for the Jacobites during the Glorious Revolution.
A Royal charter is granted to the Bank of England.
The Russian Navy achieves its first significant victory in the naval battle of Gangut against the Swedish Navy near the Hanko Peninsula.
The Second Continental Congress passes legislation establishing an hospital for an army consisting of 20,000 men.
British and French fleets fight to a standoff during the American Revolution.
The first U.S. federal government agency, the Department of Foreign Affairs, is established; it is later renamed the Department of State.
Maximilien Robespierre is arrested after encouraging the execution of more than 17,000 enemies of the Revolution.

Notes: The event is considered the deadliest single cannon shot in U.S. history.
Description: The Battle of Negro Fort ends when a hot shot cannonball fired by U.S. Navy Gunboat No. 154 explodes the fort's powder magazine, killing approximately 275.
Sixty-eight men hold out for eight days against 2,500 to 3,000 mutinying sepoys and 8,000 irregular forces.
Welsh settlers arrive at Chubut in Argentina.
The first permanent transatlantic telegraph cable is successfully completed between Valentia Island, Ireland, and Heart's Content, Newfoundland.
Afghan forces led by Mohammad Ayub Khan defeat the British Army near Maiwand, Afghanistan, during the Second Anglo-Afghan War.
Pope Felix III excommunicated Patriarch Acacius of Constantinople over his support for the Henoticon and the removal of Patriarch John Talaia, leading to the Acacian Schism.
People involved: Pope Felix III; Acacius; John Talaia

Description: Troops of the Republic of Pisa and the Republic of Florence clashed in the Battle of Cascina.
Historical entity: Republic of Pisa; Republic of Florence

Description: Timur, ruler of the Timurid Empire, defeated the forces of Ottoman sultan Bayezid I.
Henry VIII of England married his fifth wife, Catherine Howard.
People involved: Henry VIII of England; Catherine Howard

Description: Thomas Cromwell was executed after being condemned untried under a bill of attainder.
The Spaniards founded the La Laguna encomienda, now known as Laguna province, as one of the oldest encomiendas in the Philippines.
During the Eighty Years' War, Spanish forces captured the strategic Dutch fortress of Schenkenschans.
The Battle of Warsaw began during the Second Northern War.
The constitution of the province of Cantabria was ratified at the Assembly Hall in Bárcena la Puente, Reocín, Spain.
Maximilien Robespierre and Louis Antoine de Saint-Just were executed by guillotine in Paris during the French Revolution.
People involved: Maximilien Robespierre; Louis Antoine de Saint-Just

Description: Mahmud II became Sultan of the Ottoman Empire and Caliph of Islam.
In the Peninsular War, Sir Arthur Wellesley's British, Portuguese, and Spanish army repulsed a French force led by Joseph Bonaparte.
José de San Martín declared the independence of Peru from Spain.
USS Constellation, the last all-sail warship built by the United States Navy and a current museum ship in Baltimore Harbor, was commissioned.
During the American Civil War, Confederate troops made a third unsuccessful attempt under General John Bell Hood to stop Union forces led by General William T. Sherman from approaching Atlanta.
People involved: John Bell Hood; William T. Sherman

Description: At age 18, Vinnie Ream became the first and youngest female artist to receive a commission from the United States government for a statue of Abraham Lincoln.
Event title: Vinnie Ream Receives Federal Statue Commission

Description: The Fourteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution was certified, establishing African American citizenship and guaranteeing due process of law.

Notes: Magnitude is given as a range in the source.
Description: An earthquake measuring magnitude 4.3–5.2 struck the Italian island of Ischia, killing over 2,300 people.
The city of Miami was incorporated.
The Australasian Antarctic Expedition began when the SY Aurora departed London.
The Neo-Babylonian Empire sacks Jerusalem and destroys the First Temple.
Event title: Sack of Jerusalem and destruction of the First Temple

Description: The Praetorian Guard revolts against emperors Balbinus and Pupienus and arrests them.
Pakal ascends the throne of Palenque at the age of 12.
Saracen raiders under Leo of Tripoli sack Thessaloniki after a short siege and plunder it for a week.
Lombard forces under King Rudolph II and Adalbert I defeat the dethroned Emperor Berengar I of Italy at Firenzuola.
People involved: Rudolph II; Adalbert I; Berengar I

Description: Byzantine emperor Basil II inflicts a decisive defeat on the Bulgarian army; the reported treatment of prisoners is later associated with Tsar Samuil’s death.
Count Dirk III defeats an army sent by Emperor Henry II.
King Olaf II fights and dies while trying to regain his Norwegian throne from the Danes.
The Siege of Damascus ends in a decisive crusader defeat and leads to the disintegration of the Second Crusade.
Event title: End of the Siege of Damascus

Description: The widowed Mary, Queen of Scots marries Henry Stuart, Lord Darnley, Duke of Albany, at Holyrood Palace in a Catholic ceremony.
Event title: Marriage of Mary, Queen of Scots, and Henry Stuart
People involved: Mary, Queen of Scots; Henry Stuart

Description: The infant James VI is crowned King of Scotland at Stirling.
English naval forces under Lord Charles Howard and Sir Francis Drake defeat the Spanish Armada off Gravelines.
Elizabeth I visits Harefield Place at Hillingdon, where the Harefield Entertainment is performed.
France wins a victory over Allied forces in the Netherlands.
George Washington appoints William Tudor as Judge Advocate of the Continental Army.
Event title: Founding of the U.S. Army Judge Advocate General's Corps

Description: Augustin Fresnel submits his prizewinning memoir on the diffraction of light, accounting for how light spreads into shadows and supporting the wave theory of light.
An Egyptian army under Ibrahim Pascha defeats a larger Ottoman army at Belen Pass.
The Arc de Triomphe is inaugurated in Paris.
Event title: Inauguration of the Arc de Triomphe

Description: An unsuccessful nationalist revolt against British rule in County Tipperary is put down by police.
Annibale de Gasparis discovers asteroid 15 Eunomia.

Notes: The source lists the event under July 30.
Description: Vitalian was elected pope following the death of Pope Eugene I in the previous month.
Date certainty: year and month unspecified; July 30 listing

Description: Baghdad is founded.
The Mor Bar Sauma Monastery is destroyed by a fire.
Event title: Destruction of the Mor Bar Sauma Monastery

Description: A crowd of radical Hussites kills seven members of the Prague city council.
People involved: Radical Hussites; Seven members of the Prague city council

Description: Christopher Columbus lands at Guanaja in the Bay Islands off the coast of Honduras during his fourth voyage.
During the Beaver Wars, Samuel de Champlain shoots and kills two Iroquois chiefs on behalf of his native allies at Ticonderoga.
Event title: Champlain Kills Iroquois Chiefs at Ticonderoga
People involved: Samuel de Champlain; Two Iroquois chiefs

Description: The first Colonial European representative assembly in the Americas, the Virginia General Assembly, convenes for the first time in Jamestown.
Event title: First Meeting of the Virginia General Assembly

Description: An earthquake kills about 5,000 people in Gargano, Italy.
Date certainty: year and day listed; death toll approximate

Description: During the Eighty Years' War, Frederick Henry, Prince of Orange, begins the recapture of the strategically important fortress of Schenkenschans from the Spanish Army.
During the English Civil War, Scottish Covenanter forces under the Earl of Leven launch the siege of Hereford, a remaining Royalist stronghold.
The Battle of Warsaw ends with a Swedish-Brandenburger victory over a larger Polish-Lithuanian force.
Historical entity: Swedish Empire and Brandenburg against the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth

Description: Nathaniel Bacon issues the Declaration of the People of Virginia, beginning Bacon's Rebellion against Governor William Berkeley.
Event title: Declaration of the People of Virginia

Description: Baltimore, Maryland, is founded.
The first Masonic Grand Lodge in the future United States is constituted in Massachusetts.
Event title: First Masonic Grand Lodge in the Future United States

Description: In Saint Petersburg, Bartolomeo Rastrelli presents the newly built Catherine Palace to Empress Elizabeth and her courtiers.
Father Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla, leader of the Mexican insurgency, is executed by the Spanish in Chihuahua City, Mexico.
Event title: Execution of Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla

Description: Grand Combin, one of the highest summits in the Alps, is ascended for the first time.
Representatives of the United States and tribal leaders, including Chief Pocatello of the Shoshone, sign the Treaty of Box Elder.
The Valuev Circular bans the publication of religious, educational, and training books in Ukrainian in the Russian Empire.
During the American Civil War, Union forces attempt to break Confederate lines at Petersburg, Virginia, by exploding a large bomb under their trenches.
Gildo's forces were defeated by forces loyal to Western Roman Emperor Honorius under Gildo's brother Mascezel, followed by Gildo's death.
Sixtus III was elected pope following the death of Pope Celestine I four days earlier.
Antipope Constantine II was arrested by primicerius Christopher and Lombard troops sent to aid him by King Desiderius.

Notes: Traditional Japanese date.
Description: The oldest recorded eruption of Mount Fuji occurred.
Event title: Oldest recorded eruption of Mount Fuji
Original date: Sixth day of the seventh month of the first year of the Ten'o era, 781

Description: Pope Sergius IV became the 142nd pope, succeeding Pope John XVIII.
John Komnenos the Fat attempted to usurp the throne of Alexios III Angelos.
Event title: Attempted usurpation by John Komnenos the Fat
People involved: John Komnenos the Fat; Alexios III Angelos

Notes: Hundred Years' War.
Description: A Franco-Scottish army was defeated by Anglo-Burgundian forces at Cravant on the banks of the River Yonne.
Jacques Cœur was arrested by order of Charles VII of France.
All remaining Jews were expelled from Spain when the Alhambra Decree took effect.
During his third voyage to the Western Hemisphere, Christopher Columbus became the first European to discover the island of Trinidad.
Maurice, Prince of Orange, disbanded the waardgelders militia in Utrecht, a pivotal event in the Remonstrant and Counter-Remonstrant tensions.
During the Russo-Polish War, the Russian army entered Vilnius, capital of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, and held it for six years.
Aurangzeb was proclaimed Mughal emperor of India.
The treaty of Breda ended the Second Anglo-Dutch War and granted England possession of New Amsterdam.
Daniel Defoe was placed in a pillory for seditious libel after publishing a politically satirical pamphlet, but was pelted with flowers.
Event title: Daniel Defoe placed in a pillory

Description: Eleven of twelve ships from a Spanish treasure fleet sank in a storm off the coast of Florida after leaving Havana.
Charles Albert of Bavaria invaded Upper Austria and Bohemia.
Event title: Charles Albert invades Upper Austria and Bohemia

Description: Odawa Chief Pontiac's forces defeated British troops at the Battle of Bloody Run during Pontiac's War.
The Second Continental Congress accepted Gilbert du Motier, Marquis de Lafayette's services and granted him the rank and commission of major-general of the United States.
People involved: Gilbert du Motier, Marquis de Lafayette

Description: The first U.S. patent was issued to inventor Samuel Hopkins for a potash process.
